flashcards.q: Which Compute Engine machine families are eligible for sustained-use discounts, and which current-generation families are NOT?
flashcards.a: Eligible: N1, N2, N2D, C2, M1, M2, sole-tenant nodes, GPUs attached to N1. NOT eligible (zero automatic discount): E2, C3/C3D, C4/C4A/C4D, N4/N4D/N4A, H3/H4D, Z3, T2A/T2D -- these require a CUD to get any discount regardless of runtime.

flashcards.q: How does the sustained-use discount ramp within a billing month?
flashcards.a: It ramps at usage thresholds of 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% of the month. For a 30%-max resource: 50% month usage = ~10% effective discount, 75% = ~20%, 100% = the full 30%.

flashcards.q: What discount range do resource-based CUDs offer, and what's the tradeoff?
flashcards.a: Up to 55% off for most machine series, up to 70% for memory-optimized (M1-M4), for a 1- or 3-year commitment. Tradeoff: pinned to a specific machine type/region/quantity, billed whether used or not, and cannot be canceled.

flashcards.q: What is a compute flexible CUD and what's the memory-optimized 1-year trap?
flashcards.a: A spend-based commitment with no machine-type/region pinning, applying across Compute Engine, GKE, and Cloud Run. General purpose: 28% (1yr)/46% (3yr). Trap: memory-optimized (M1-M4) gets 0% discount at 1 year -- only a 3-year term unlocks any discount (63%).

flashcards.q: What is the GKE cluster management fee and what does the free tier cover?
flashcards.a: A flat $0.10/cluster/hour applies to every GKE cluster (Standard or Autopilot, zonal or regional). The free tier gives $74.40/month credit, roughly one free zonal Standard or Autopilot cluster -- it never applies to regional cluster fees or compute charges.

flashcards.q: Describe GKE Autopilot's two billing models and what triggers each.
flashcards.a: General-purpose Pods (default platform, Balanced/Scale-Out classes): Pod-based billing, charged for the resource REQUEST in 1-second increments with no minimum, only while Running/ContainerCreating. Pods requesting specific hardware (GPU, named machine series): node-based billing, charged for the whole provisioned node plus an Autopilot management premium.

flashcards.q: When should you choose GKE Standard over Autopilot?
flashcards.a: When the workload needs privileged containers/hostPath access, custom DaemonSets beyond what Autopilot permits, fine-grained node-level tuning, or specific GPU/TPU node topologies -- Autopilot enforces stricter security defaults and removes direct node control. Google's default recommendation for new clusters is Autopilot first.

flashcards.q: What happens to sustained-use discount accrual when a project moves between Cloud Billing accounts?
flashcards.a: Sustained resource usage time resets to zero on the new billing account -- it is not carried forward. Google recommends making billing account changes on the first day of a month to minimize the impact.

flashcards.q: Do sustained-use discounts and committed-use discounts stack on the same usage?
flashcards.a: No. SUDs don't apply to usage already covered by a CUD -- CUD coverage takes priority and SUD applies only to the remaining uncommitted usage on eligible machine families.

flashcards.q: How does GKE Autopilot's Pod-based billing differ from Fargate's task billing philosophically?
flashcards.a: Both bill for provisioned/requested capacity rather than measured consumption, but Autopilot bills only while a Pod is Running/ContainerCreating (not scheduled or terminated Pods) in 1-second increments with no minimum, while Fargate bills continuously for provisioned vCPU/memory per task regardless of load fluctuation, with per-second billing and a one-minute minimum on the underlying resource.
